aspects.says: An expression body fits a void method only if it is a statement expression; a block is value-compatible only if every return carries a value and its end can't be reached.
basis: section:A Body's Shape Decides Whether It Returns a Value, Nothing, or Either

aspects.says: An implicitly typed lambda, var included, with an expression body is ambiguous between same-arity overloads on different functional interfaces; declared types or a cast fix one call, a distinct method name fixes every caller.
basis: section:An Implicitly Typed Lambda Can't Choose Between Overloads of the Same Arity

aspects.says: A cast to an intersection type such as (Runnable & Serializable) gives a lambda both interfaces, so it can be serialized.
basis: section:An Implicitly Typed Lambda Can't Choose Between Overloads of the Same Arity
aspects.reason: serializing a lambda is a one-line cast whose only wrong form fails with NotSerializableException at once; the page shows the run, and a practice would only repeat it

aspects.says: A lambda can't implement a generic functional method; a method reference, a class or a generic interface can.
basis: section:A Lambda Can't Implement a Generic Method

aspects.says: A lambda's parameters are all inferred, all declared, or all var; one list can't mix the forms, and an annotation or final needs a declared type or var.
basis: section:A Lambda's Parameters Are All Inferred or All Declared
aspects.reason: a compile-time rule: every wrong solution fails to compile, so no running test can tell it from a missing one; the quiz's first question uses its consequence that var still counts as inferred

aspects.says: When a body fits both a void and a value-returning interface and its parameter types are known, the value-returning overload is chosen, so braces or a return decide what submit's Future holds and whether a checked exception reaches it.
basis: section:When a Body Fits Both, the Overload That Returns a Value Wins
